A Core NATS message reaches whoever is subscribed /// at that moment and is not stored, so `retry` here delivers nothing again: the message is /// processed at most once. #[subscriber("orders.shipped")] async fn notify(order: &Shipped) -> HandlerOutcome { match send_mail(&order.email).await { Ok(()) => HandlerOutcome::ack(), Err(err) => { tracing::error!(order.id, %err, "the shipping notice is lost"); HandlerOutcome::retry() } } } examples/manual/nats_settlement_core.rs /// Mails the customer once the order ships. dead_letter(subject) names the subject a spent delivery is published to; a capped JetStream consumer with none terminates it. It follows max_attempts(n) at the mount site. When a retry would make the delivery the n-th one, the framework settles it and publishes it to the dead-letter subject instead, payload and headers as they arrived. On a JetStream consumer the delivery is then terminated, so the server delivers it no more. NATS has no dead-letter mechanism of its own, so the same path serves both models, and a warning names the subscription that gave up. The copy carries RETRY_COUNT_HEADER: on a Core subject it says how many deliveries the message had; on a JetStream consumer the server counted them, and the header reads 1. A cap without a dead-letter subject terminates the spent JetStream delivery, and ends the Core one. The dead-letter subject is an ordinary subject: a subscription of this service or of another one reads it. It stays outside every pattern a subscription of the service reads, or the spent message arrives back at a handler.

The dead-letter subject is read by an ordinary subscription. Macros Manual examples/nats_retry.rs /// The dead-letter subject is read by an ordinary subscription. The retry-count header says how /// many deliveries the payment had before it was carried here. #[subscriber("payments.dead")] async fn on_dead_letter(payment: &Payment, ctx: &mut Context<'_>) -> HandlerOutcome { let deliveries = ctx.headers().get_str(RETRY_COUNT_HEADER).unwrap_or("1"); tracing::error!(payment.id, deliveries, "payment dead-lettered"); HandlerOutcome::ack() } examples/manual/nats_retry.rs /// The dead-letter subject is read by an ordinary subscription. The retry-count header says how /// many deliveries the payment had before it was carried here. struct OnDeadLetter; impl Handle<Payment> for OnDeadLetter { fn handle( &self, payment: &Payment, _outs: &(), ctx: &mut Context<'_>, ) -> impl Future<Output = Result<(), HandlerOutcome>> { let deliveries = ctx.headers().get_str(RETRY_COUNT_HEADER).unwrap_or("1"); tracing::error!(payment.id, deliveries, "payment dead-lettered"); ready(Ok(())) } }

A pattern names no subject of its own, so out_retry(Publish).to(subject) says where its delayed copies go; without it the app refuses to start. A CoreWildcard reads every subject its pattern matches, and a copy has to go to one of them. This crate does not take the pattern itself as a destination, so the mount site names the subject. A registration over a pattern that names no subject fails the start with an error naming the subscription. The service reports the gap at startup instead of losing every delayed message once it runs. out_retry binds the Retry slot, the one the framework publishes its copies through, to a policy; Publish is plain Core NATS. .to(subject) names the subject; a publish transform that declares Names can choose one per delivery instead. A subject the pattern matches brings the copy back to the same handler. The dead-letter subject stays outside the pattern, or the spent message comes back too. A CoreSubject and a JetStreamSubject name their own destination, so they need no out_retry; on them the slot only changes the policy or adds a transform.

Entries of every region are audited again a minute later through audits.retry, which the pattern reads. Macros Manual examples/nats_settlement_out_retry.rs /// Audits the entries of every region, `audits.eu`, `audits.us` and the rest. #[subscriber(CoreWildcard::new("audits.*"))] async fn audit(entry: &Entry) -> HandlerOutcome { if entry.posted { return HandlerOutcome::ack(); } tracing::info!(entry.id, "not posted yet, auditing again later"); HandlerOutcome::retry_after(RECHECK) } #[ruststream::app] fn app() -> impl App { RustStream::new(AppInfo::new("audit", "0.1.0")).with_broker( NatsBroker::new("nats://localhost:4222"), |b| { // The copies go to "audits.retry", which the pattern reads, so they come back here. // The dead-letter subject is outside the pattern, so a spent entry does not. b.include(audit) .max_attempts(nonzero!(3u32)) .dead_letter("dead.audits") .out_retry(Publish) .to("audits.retry"); }, ) } examples/manual/nats_settlement_out_retry.rs /// Audits the entries of every region, `audits.eu`, `audits.us` and the rest. struct Audit; impl Handle<Entry> for Audit { fn handle( &self, entry: &Entry, _outs: &(), _ctx: &mut Context<'_>, ) -> impl Future<Output = Result<(), HandlerOutcome>> { if entry.posted { return ready(Ok(())); } tracing::info!(entry.id, "not posted yet, auditing again later"); ready(Err(HandlerOutcome::retry_after(RECHECK))) } } fn app() -> impl App { RustStream::new(AppInfo::new("audit", "0.1.0")).with_broker( NatsBroker::new("nats://localhost:4222"), |b| { // The copies go to "audits.retry", which the pattern reads, so they come back here. // The dead-letter subject is outside the pattern, so a spent entry does not. b.include(subscriber(CoreWildcard::new("audits.*"), Audit).build()) .max_attempts(nonzero!(3u32)) .dead_letter("dead.audits") .out_retry(Publish) .to("audits.retry"); }, ) }

max_attempts(n) caps the deliveries of one message; on JetStream it counts the server's own deliveries, on Core the copies in a header. It is declared at the mount site, and the first delivery counts as one. A JetStream consumer reports how many times it has delivered a message, so the cap reads that number. Every delivery counts: a retry, a retry_after, and a redelivery after ack_wait. A Core subject delivers each message once, so the framework counts the copies it publishes, in RETRY_COUNT_HEADER. Under a cap every retry on a Core subject travels as such a copy, an immediate one too. The delivery that reaches the cap goes to the dead-letter subject, or is terminated when the mount site names none. The cap is the framework's own: the consumer the crate creates leaves max_deliver at the server's default, unlimited, so the server delivers a retried message again until the cap ends it.

Five deliveries of one payment, on a Core subject and on a stream; the fifth that still fails goes to payments.dead. Macros Manual examples/nats_retry.rs #[ruststream::app] fn app() -> impl App { RustStream::new(AppInfo::new("payments", "0.1.0")).with_broker( NatsBroker::new("nats://localhost:4222"), |b| { // Five deliveries of one payment, the first included; the fifth that still fails goes // to "payments.dead" instead, payload and headers as they arrived. b.include(reconcile) .max_attempts(nonzero!(5u32)) .dead_letter("payments.dead"); b.include(store) .max_attempts(nonzero!(5u32)) .dead_letter("payments.dead"); b.include(on_dead_letter); }, ) } examples/manual/nats_retry.rs fn app() -> impl App { RustStream::new(AppInfo::new("payments", "0.1.0")).with_broker( NatsBroker::new("nats://localhost:4222"), |b| { // Five deliveries of one payment, the first included; the fifth that still fails goes // to "payments.dead" instead, payload and headers as they arrived. b.include(subscriber("payments.settled", Reconcile).build()) .max_attempts(nonzero!(5u32)) .dead_letter("payments.dead"); let stored = JetStreamSubject::new("payments.stored", "PAYMENTS").durable("reconciler"); b.include(subscriber(stored, Reconcile).build()) .max_attempts(nonzero!(5u32)) .dead_letter("payments.dead"); b.include(subscriber("payments.dead", OnDeadLetter).build()); }, ) }

retry_after(delay) on JetStream puts the delay in the negative acknowledgement; on Core the framework publishes a copy after the delay. A JetStream consumer takes the delay as part of -NAK. The server holds the message for that long and delivers it again on the same consumer. Nothing is published, so the message keeps its stream sequence, and its delivery count rises by one. On a durable consumer the delayed message survives a restart of the service, because the server holds it. A Core subject has no acknowledgement to carry a delay. The framework waits out the delay in the service's memory and publishes a copy of the message, payload and headers, back to the subject the subscription reads. The copy carries RETRY_COUNT_HEADER, raised by one on every copy. A process that exits before the delay is over loses the copy. A CoreWildcard reads many subjects, so its mount site names where the copy goes with out_retry. A cap declared at the mount site ends the retries of one message.

A payment the ledger has not caught up with is checked again after 30 seconds, on a Core subject and on a stream. Macros Manual examples/nats_retry.rs /// The ledger has not caught up yet, so the delivery asks to come back later. On a Core subject /// the framework publishes a copy of the payment to the subject once the delay is over. #[subscriber("payments.settled")] async fn reconcile(payment: &Payment) -> HandlerOutcome { if payment.settled { return HandlerOutcome::ack(); } tracing::info!(payment.id, "not settled yet, checking again later"); HandlerOutcome::retry_after(RECHECK) } /// The same work through a stream: the delay rides the negative acknowledgement, and the server /// holds the message and delivers it again on this consumer. #[subscriber(JetStreamSubject::new("payments.stored", "PAYMENTS").durable("reconciler"))] async fn store(payment: &Payment) -> HandlerOutcome { if payment.settled { return HandlerOutcome::ack(); } tracing::info!(payment.id, "not settled yet, checking again later"); HandlerOutcome::retry_after(RECHECK) } examples/manual/nats_retry.rs /// The ledger has not caught up yet, so the delivery asks to come back later. Mounted on a Core /// subject, the framework publishes a copy of the payment to the subject once the delay is over; /// mounted on a stream consumer, the delay rides the negative acknowledgement and the server /// holds the message. struct Reconcile; impl Handle<Payment> for Reconcile { fn handle( &self, payment: &Payment, _outs: &(), _ctx: &mut Context<'_>, ) -> impl Future<Output = Result<(), HandlerOutcome>> { if payment.settled { return ready(Ok(())); } tracing::info!(payment.id, "not settled yet, checking again later"); ready(Err(HandlerOutcome::retry_after(RECHECK))) } }

A subject in #[subscriber] reads that Core NATS subject; a descriptor carries every other setting of its delivery model. #[subscriber("orders.created")] reads the subject orders.created over Core NATS, with no queue group. It is the same subscription as CoreSubject::new("orders.created"). Core NATS hands a message to whoever is subscribed at that moment and stores nothing, so a message published before the service starts never reaches it. Every other setting belongs to a descriptor, one type per delivery model: Descriptor Reads Its settings CoreSubject one Core NATS subject queue_group CoreWildcard every Core NATS subject a pattern matches queue_group JetStreamSubject a stream, through a pull consumer durable, filter_subject, deliver_policy, max_ack_pending, ack_wait, pull_expires A setting of the other model is not a method of the descriptor, so naming one does not compile. A descriptor goes where the subject goes, as the attribute's first argument. The manual form passes the subject, or the descriptor, to subscriber(source, body). The subscription's name is the subject the descriptor names: a test reads its deliveries under that name. All subscriptions of a service share the one connection of its NatsBroker.

The subject orders.created, read over Core NATS. Macros Manual examples/nats_subscriptions_name.rs /// Reads the Core NATS subject `orders.created`. #[subscriber("orders.created")] async fn place(order: &Order) -> HandlerOutcome { tracing::info!(order.id, "order placed"); HandlerOutcome::ack() } #[ruststream::app] fn app() -> impl App { RustStream::new(AppInfo::new("orders", "0.1.0")).with_broker( NatsBroker::new("nats://localhost:4222"), |b| { b.include(place); }, ) } examples/manual/nats_subscriptions_name.rs /// Reads the Core NATS subject `orders.created`. struct Place; impl Handle<Order> for Place { fn handle( &self, order: &Order, _outs: &(), _ctx: &mut Context<'_>, ) -> impl Future<Output = Result<(), HandlerOutcome>> { tracing::info!(order.id, "order placed"); ready(Ok(())) } } fn app() -> impl App { RustStream::new(AppInfo::new("orders", "0.1.0")).with_broker( NatsBroker::new("nats://localhost:4222"), |b| { b.include(subscriber("orders.created", Place).build()); }, ) }

A slice handler takes a batch: one JetStream pull fetch of the mount site's size, or a Core NATS batch the client assembles. A handler over &[T] is a batch handler, and batch(n) at the mount site is its largest batch. On a JetStreamSubject one batch is one pull request: the consumer asks the server for up to n messages. The fetch ends once it holds n, or once pull_expires runs out with fewer, 5 seconds by default. pull_expires takes a NonZeroDuration, because a fetch that expires at once would spin. Core NATS has no batch on the wire, so the client collects up to n deliveries and closes a short batch 10 ms after its first one. One outcome settles every message of the batch. A Vec<HandlerOutcome> settles message i with outcome i. In the manual form the body is an impl Handle<[T]>, where Ok(()) acknowledges the batch and Err(outcomes) settles message by message.

Three orders waiting in the stream arrive in one call. Macros Manual examples/nats_subscriptions_batches.rs /// Reconciles up to 50 orders per call; a fetch that finds fewer closes after 300 ms. #[subscriber( JetStreamSubject::new("orders.*", "ORDERS") .durable("reconciler") .pull_expires(NonZeroDuration::from_millis(nonzero!(300))) )] async fn reconcile(orders: &[Order]) -> HandlerOutcome { let total: u64 = orders.iter().map(|order| order.cents).sum(); tracing::info!(count = orders.len(), total, "orders reconciled"); HandlerOutcome::ack() } #[ruststream::app] fn app() -> impl App { RustStream::new(AppInfo::new("reconciliation", "0.1.0")).with_broker( NatsBroker::new("nats://localhost:4222"), |b| { b.include(reconcile.batch(nonzero!(50))); }, ) } examples/manual/nats_subscriptions_batches.rs /// Reconciles up to 50 orders per call; a fetch that finds fewer closes after 300 ms. struct Reconcile; impl Handle<[Order]> for Reconcile { fn handle( &self, orders: &[Order], _outs: &(), _ctx: &mut Context<'_>, ) -> impl Future<Output = Result<(), Vec<HandlerOutcome>>> { let total: u64 = orders.iter().map(|order| order.cents).sum(); tracing::info!(count = orders.len(), total, "orders reconciled"); ready(Ok(())) } } fn app() -> impl App { RustStream::new(AppInfo::new("reconciliation", "0.1.0")).with_broker( NatsBroker::new("nats://localhost:4222"), |b| { let orders = JetStreamSubject::new("orders.*", "ORDERS") .durable("reconciler") .pull_expires(NonZeroDuration::from_millis(nonzero!(300))); b.include(subscriber(orders, Reconcile).batch(nonzero!(50)).build()); }, ) }

CoreSubject reads one Core NATS subject; it stores nothing, and a delayed copy of a delivery is published back to the subject itself. CoreSubject::new takes the subject, and its one setting is the queue group. The server delivers a message to every subscription on the subject at that moment and keeps nothing for later. A subject is published to and subscribed to under one name, so a delayed retry needs nothing from the mount site. A retry_after(delay) settles the delivery, and after the delay the runtime publishes a copy back to the subject. The copy waits in the service's memory, so a process that exits before the timer fires loses it. A subject with * or > in it is a pattern, which is CoreWildcard; CoreSubject given one stops the service at startup. An empty subject stops it too. A stream that keeps messages for a consumer is JetStreamSubject.

A payment the bank has not cleared yet comes back to payments.captured after 30 seconds. Macros Manual examples/nats_subscriptions_core.rs /// Books a cleared payment; one the bank has not cleared yet comes back in 30 seconds, as a copy /// published to `payments.captured` again. #[subscriber(CoreSubject::new("payments.captured"))] async fn book(payment: &Payment) -> HandlerOutcome { if !payment.cleared { tracing::info!(payment.id, "not cleared yet, checking again later"); return HandlerOutcome::retry_after(RECHECK); } tracing::info!(payment.id, "payment booked"); HandlerOutcome::ack() } #[ruststream::app] fn app() -> impl App { RustStream::new(AppInfo::new("ledger", "0.1.0")).with_broker( NatsBroker::new("nats://localhost:4222"), |b| { b.include(book); }, ) } examples/manual/nats_subscriptions_core.rs /// Books a cleared payment; one the bank has not cleared yet comes back in 30 seconds, as a copy /// published to `payments.captured` again. struct Book; impl Handle<Payment> for Book { fn handle( &self, payment: &Payment, _outs: &(), _ctx: &mut Context<'_>, ) -> impl Future<Output = Result<(), HandlerOutcome>> { if !payment.cleared { tracing::info!(payment.id, "not cleared yet, checking again later"); return ready(Err(HandlerOutcome::retry_after(RECHECK))); } tracing::info!(payment.id, "payment booked"); ready(Ok(())) } } fn app() -> impl App { RustStream::new(AppInfo::new("ledger", "0.1.0")).with_broker( NatsBroker::new("nats://localhost:4222"), |b| { b.include(subscriber(CoreSubject::new("payments.captured"), Book).build()); }, ) }

CoreWildcard reads every Core NATS subject a pattern matches, * for one token and > for the rest, and the mount site names where a delayed copy goes. A subject is a list of tokens separated by dots. orders.* matches orders.created and orders.cancelled, but not orders.eu.created. orders.> matches all three, and > alone matches every subject. CoreWildcard::new takes the pattern, and its one setting is the queue group. The subscription's name is the pattern itself. A pattern names many subjects and none of them in particular, so the crate does not choose where a delayed retry copy goes. The mount site names that subject with out_retry(Publish).to(subject). A registration over a pattern that names none stops the service at startup, with an error naming the subscription. A subject the pattern matches brings the copy back to the same handler.

Every one-token order event is audited, and a delayed copy goes to orders.audit. Macros Manual examples/nats_subscriptions_wildcard.rs /// Audits every one-token order event: `orders.created`, `orders.cancelled`, and the rest. #[subscriber(CoreWildcard::new("orders.*"))] async fn audit(event: &OrderEvent) -> HandlerOutcome { tracing::info!(event.order_id, "order event audited"); HandlerOutcome::ack() } #[ruststream::app] fn app() -> impl App { RustStream::new(AppInfo::new("audit", "0.1.0")).with_broker( NatsBroker::new("nats://localhost:4222"), |b| { // A pattern is no destination, so the mount site names where a delayed copy goes. b.include(audit).out_retry(Publish).to("orders.audit"); }, ) } examples/manual/nats_subscriptions_wildcard.rs /// Audits every one-token order event: `orders.created`, `orders.cancelled`, and the rest. struct Audit; impl Handle<OrderEvent> for Audit { fn handle( &self, event: &OrderEvent, _outs: &(), _ctx: &mut Context<'_>, ) -> impl Future<Output = Result<(), HandlerOutcome>> { tracing::info!(event.order_id, "order event audited"); ready(Ok(())) } } fn app() -> impl App { RustStream::new(AppInfo::new("audit", "0.1.0")).with_broker( NatsBroker::new("nats://localhost:4222"), |b| { // A pattern is no destination, so the mount site names where a delayed copy goes. b.include(subscriber(CoreWildcard::new("orders.*"), Audit).build()) .out_retry(Publish) .to("orders.audit"); }, ) }

DeliverPolicy says where a newly created consumer starts: all, new, last, last per subject, a sequence or a time. deliver_policy sets it on the descriptor. The type is the one async-nats defines, re-exported by the crate. All, the default, starts with the oldest message the stream holds. New starts with the first message published after the consumer was created. Last starts with the newest message of the stream, and LastPerSubject with the newest message of each subject the filter matches. ByStartSequence starts at a stream sequence, and ByStartTime at the first message stored at or after a time. The policy applies once, when the consumer is created. A durable consumer that already exists resumes from its own position. An ephemeral consumer is created on every startup, so it starts from its policy each time.

A live ticker starts with the next price, and the prices the stream held before it started stay behind. Macros Manual examples/nats_subscriptions_deliver.rs /// A live ticker: each new consumer starts with the next price, not with the stream's history. #[subscriber(JetStreamSubject::new("prices.*", "PRICES").deliver_policy(DeliverPolicy::New))] async fn tick(price: &Price) -> HandlerOutcome { tracing::info!(price.product, price.cents, "price changed"); HandlerOutcome::ack() } #[ruststream::app] fn app() -> impl App { RustStream::new(AppInfo::new("ticker", "0.1.0")).with_broker( NatsBroker::new("nats://localhost:4222"), |b| { b.include(tick); }, ) } examples/manual/nats_subscriptions_deliver.rs /// A live ticker: each new consumer starts with the next price, not with the stream's history. struct Tick; impl Handle<Price> for Tick { fn handle( &self, price: &Price, _outs: &(), _ctx: &mut Context<'_>, ) -> impl Future<Output = Result<(), HandlerOutcome>> { tracing::info!(price.product, price.cents, "price changed"); ready(Ok(())) } } fn prices() -> JetStreamSubject { JetStreamSubject::new("prices.*", "PRICES").deliver_policy(DeliverPolicy::New) } fn app() -> impl App { RustStream::new(AppInfo::new("ticker", "0.1.0")).with_broker( NatsBroker::new("nats://localhost:4222"), |b| { b.include(subscriber(prices(), Tick).build()); }, ) }

durable names a JetStream consumer: the server keeps its position across restarts, and subscriptions sharing it take messages in turn. A named consumer lives on the server, apart from any subscription. It remembers which messages were acknowledged, so a restarted service resumes after the last one and reads what arrived while it was down. A consumer without a name is ephemeral and starts from its deliver policy on every startup. Every replica of a service that reads through one durable shares its messages: each message goes to one of them, as in a queue group. At startup the subscription creates the consumer, or updates it when it exists. So the settings the last subscription opened with are the consumer's settings, and replicas that share a durable name one filter and one policy.

Every replica bills through the consumer billing, and a restarted service resumes where the consumer stopped. Macros Manual examples/nats_subscriptions_durable.rs /// Every replica reads through the consumer `billing`: each invoice is billed once, and a /// restarted service resumes where the consumer stopped. #[subscriber(JetStreamSubject::new("invoices.*", "INVOICES").durable("billing"))] async fn bill(invoice: &Invoice) -> HandlerOutcome { tracing::info!(invoice.id, "invoice billed"); HandlerOutcome::ack() } #[ruststream::app] fn app() -> impl App { RustStream::new(AppInfo::new("billing", "0.1.0")).with_broker( NatsBroker::new("nats://localhost:4222"), |b| { b.include(bill); }, ) } examples/manual/nats_subscriptions_durable.rs /// Every replica reads through the consumer `billing`: each invoice is billed once, and a /// restarted service resumes where the consumer stopped. struct Bill; impl Handle<Invoice> for Bill { fn handle( &self, invoice: &Invoice, _outs: &(), _ctx: &mut Context<'_>, ) -> impl Future<Output = Result<(), HandlerOutcome>> { tracing::info!(invoice.id, "invoice billed"); ready(Ok(())) } } fn app() -> impl App { RustStream::new(AppInfo::new("billing", "0.1.0")).with_broker( NatsBroker::new("nats://localhost:4222"), |b| { let invoices = JetStreamSubject::new("invoices.*", "INVOICES").durable("billing"); b.include(subscriber(invoices, Bill).build()); }, ) }

filter_subject narrows the subjects of the stream a consumer reads; it defaults to the subject the descriptor names. A stream often stores several kinds of message under one prefix, such as every order event under orders.>. The consumer's filter decides which of them it is handed; the server skips the rest for this consumer. Without filter_subject the filter is the subject given to JetStreamSubject::new. With it, the descriptor's subject stays the subscription's name, and the filter decides what arrives. A filter may be a pattern with * and >. A durable consumer has one filter, the one its last subscription opened with.

The stream ORDERS stores every order event, and the refunds consumer reads orders.refunded only. Macros Manual examples/nats_subscriptions_filter.rs /// Reads only the refunds of the `ORDERS` stream, which stores every order event. #[subscriber( JetStreamSubject::new("orders.>", "ORDERS") .durable("refunds") .filter_subject("orders.refunded") )] async fn refund(order: &Order) -> HandlerOutcome { tracing::info!(order.id, "order refunded"); HandlerOutcome::ack() } #[ruststream::app] fn app() -> impl App { RustStream::new(AppInfo::new("refunds", "0.1.0")).with_broker( NatsBroker::new("nats://localhost:4222"), |b| { b.include(refund); }, ) } examples/manual/nats_subscriptions_filter.rs /// Reads only the refunds of the `ORDERS` stream, which stores every order event. struct Refund; impl Handle<Order> for Refund { fn handle( &self, order: &Order, _outs: &(), _ctx: &mut Context<'_>, ) -> impl Future<Output = Result<(), HandlerOutcome>> { tracing::info!(order.id, "order refunded"); ready(Ok(())) } } fn app() -> impl App { RustStream::new(AppInfo::new("refunds", "0.1.0")).with_broker( NatsBroker::new("nats://localhost:4222"), |b| { let refunds = JetStreamSubject::new("orders.>", "ORDERS") .durable("refunds") .filter_subject("orders.refunded"); b.include(subscriber(refunds, Refund).build()); }, ) }

JetStreamSubject reads a stream through a pull consumer; the stream exists on the server before the service starts. A stream stores the messages published to its subjects, and a consumer reads them at its own pace. JetStreamSubject::new(subject, stream) takes the subject to read and the name of the stream that stores it. At startup the subscription finds the stream and creates its consumer; a stream the server does not have stops the service. The crate creates no stream: the service's deployment does, for example with nats stream add. Without durable the consumer is ephemeral, and the server discards it once the subscription closes. Each delivery settles on the server: an ack acknowledges it, and a retry or a delay is a negative acknowledgement the server acts on. The settings and their defaults: Setting Default What it does durable none, an ephemeral consumer names the consumer, which keeps its position across restarts filter_subject the subject narrows what the consumer reads from the stream deliver_policy DeliverPolicy::All where a new consumer starts max_ack_pending 1024 how many deliveries the consumer holds unacknowledged ack_wait 30 seconds how long the server waits for a settlement before it delivers again pull_expires 5 seconds how long one fetch of a batch waits for messages The subscription's name is the subject the descriptor names. A delivery carries its place in the stream, which a handler reads through the context keys.

The stream ORDERS stores orders.*, and an ephemeral consumer reads it. Macros Manual examples/nats_subscriptions_jetstream.rs /// Reads `orders.*` from the stream `ORDERS`; the ack settles each order on the server. #[subscriber(JetStreamSubject::new("orders.*", "ORDERS"))] async fn ship(order: &Order) -> HandlerOutcome { tracing::info!(order.id, "order shipped"); HandlerOutcome::ack() } #[ruststream::app] fn app() -> impl App { RustStream::new(AppInfo::new("shipping", "0.1.0")).with_broker( NatsBroker::new("nats://localhost:4222"), |b| { b.include(ship); }, ) } examples/manual/nats_subscriptions_jetstream.rs /// Reads `orders.*` from the stream `ORDERS`; `Ok` acknowledges each order on the server. struct Ship; impl Handle<Order> for Ship { fn handle( &self, order: &Order, _outs: &(), _ctx: &mut Context<'_>, ) -> impl Future<Output = Result<(), HandlerOutcome>> { tracing::info!(order.id, "order shipped"); ready(Ok(())) } } fn app() -> impl App { RustStream::new(AppInfo::new("shipping", "0.1.0")).with_broker( NatsBroker::new("nats://localhost:4222"), |b| { let orders = JetStreamSubject::new("orders.*", "ORDERS"); b.include(subscriber(orders, Ship).build()); }, ) }

The nats-partition-key header keys the lanes of workers(n, by_key): messages sharing a key run on one lane, in order. workers(n, by_key) runs n sequential lanes in one subscription. Messages with one key run in order on one lane, and different keys run at once. NATS has no partitions or message keys, so the key travels in the nats-partition-key header. The sender sets it: any NATS client writes the header, and a RustStream message type declares it in its typed header contract. The value is text, because a NATS header is; a value that is not a single line of UTF-8 fails the publish. A message without the header has no key and rotates over the lanes. The lanes work the same on Core NATS and on a stream. The manual form writes the lanes as workers_by_key(n) on the mount chain.

Two tenants' orders, each order a second of work: the tenants run side by side, two seconds in all. max_ack_pending caps how many unacknowledged deliveries the server lets a consumer hold at once; the default is 1024. A delivery is pending from the moment the server hands it out until it is settled. Once the consumer holds that many, the server stops delivering until a settlement frees a place. The cap belongs to the consumer, so every subscription that shares a durable counts against one cap. It bounds the work in flight from the server's side, whatever the service does. workers(n) runs up to n handlers at once in one subscription; with a cap below n, the cap is the limit. A delivery the consumer holds counts against its ack_wait from the moment it is handed out, so a large cap over slow handlers lets deliveries wait out their ack_wait and come back. The cap is enforced by the server, so a test of it runs against a live server.

Six workers render reports, and the server hands out two at a time. Macros Manual examples/nats_subscriptions_pending.rs /// Six workers, but the server hands out at most two reports before they are acknowledged, so /// two render at a time. #[subscriber( JetStreamSubject::new("reports.requested", "REPORTS") .durable("renderers") .max_ack_pending(2), workers(6) )] async fn produce(report: &Report) -> HandlerOutcome { render(report).await; HandlerOutcome::ack() } #[ruststream::app] fn app() -> impl App { RustStream::new(AppInfo::new("reports", "0.1.0")).with_broker( NatsBroker::new("nats://localhost:4222"), |b| { b.include(produce); }, ) } examples/manual/nats_subscriptions_pending.rs /// Six workers, but the server hands out at most two reports before they are acknowledged, so /// two render at a time. struct Produce; impl Handle<Report> for Produce { async fn handle( &self, report: &Report, _outs: &(), _ctx: &mut Context<'_>, ) -> Result<(), HandlerOutcome> { render(report).await; Ok(()) } } fn reports() -> JetStreamSubject { JetStreamSubject::new("reports.requested", "REPORTS") .durable("renderers") .max_ack_pending(2) } fn app() -> impl App { RustStream::new(AppInfo::new("reports", "0.1.0")).with_broker( NatsBroker::new("nats://localhost:4222"), |b| { b.include(subscriber(reports(), Produce).workers(nonzero!(6)).build()); }, ) }

queue_group puts a Core NATS subscription in a queue group: each message goes to one member, and one name is one group across subjects. Without a group, every subscription on a subject receives every message. Replicas of a service that subscribe in one group share the messages instead, and the server picks one member for each. A subscription outside the group still receives everything, so an audit can read beside the workers. The server keys a group by its name alone, so subscriptions with one group name on two subjects or patterns are one group. A message both of them match is delivered once, to one member. CoreSubject::queue_group and CoreWildcard::queue_group take the same name. Core NATS keeps nothing for a group: a message published while no member is subscribed is lost. On a stream the same sharing comes from a durable consumer that several subscriptions read through.

Every replica fulfils orders in the group fulfilment, and the audit reads every order outside it. Macros Manual examples/nats_subscriptions_queue.rs /// Every replica of the service joins `fulfilment`, so each order is fulfilled once. #[subscriber(CoreSubject::new("orders.created").queue_group("fulfilment"))] async fn fulfil(order: &Order) -> HandlerOutcome { tracing::info!(order.id, "order fulfilled"); HandlerOutcome::ack() } /// Outside the group: the audit reads every order. #[subscriber(CoreWildcard::new("orders.*"))] async fn audit(order: &Order) -> HandlerOutcome { tracing::info!(order.id, "order audited"); HandlerOutcome::ack() } #[ruststream::app] fn app() -> impl App { RustStream::new(AppInfo::new("fulfilment", "0.1.0")).with_broker( NatsBroker::new("nats://localhost:4222"), |b| { b.include(fulfil); b.include(audit).out_retry(Publish).to("orders.audit"); }, ) } examples/manual/nats_subscriptions_queue.rs /// Every replica of the service joins `fulfilment`, so each order is fulfilled once. struct Fulfil; impl Handle<Order> for Fulfil { fn handle( &self, order: &Order, _outs: &(), _ctx: &mut Context<'_>, ) -> impl Future<Output = Result<(), HandlerOutcome>> { tracing::info!(order.id, "order fulfilled"); ready(Ok(())) } } /// Outside the group: the audit reads every order. struct Audit; impl Handle<Order> for Audit { fn handle( &self, order: &Order, _outs: &(), _ctx: &mut Context<'_>, ) -> impl Future<Output = Result<(), HandlerOutcome>> { tracing::info!(order.id, "order audited"); ready(Ok(())) } } fn app() -> impl App { RustStream::new(AppInfo::new("fulfilment", "0.1.0")).with_broker( NatsBroker::new("nats://localhost:4222"), |b| { let fulfilment = CoreSubject::new("orders.created").queue_group("fulfilment"); b.include(subscriber(fulfilment, Fulfil).build()); b.include(subscriber(CoreWildcard::new("orders.*"), Audit).build()) .out_retry(Publish) .to("orders.audit"); }, ) }

TestApp::start connects NatsBroker in process: subjects, queue groups, streams, consumers and request-reply, with no server. A test hands the harness the app main runs, unchanged, and addresses the broker by its production type, tb.broker::<NatsBroker>(). The testing feature in [dev-dependencies] adds the in-process mode, and turns on the core's harness with it. The in-process mode has no settings of its own. It parses the addresses as the client parses them, so an address the client refuses fails TestApp::start. It reads the two connection options that change what the server delivers, no_echo and the inbox prefix. It routes as a server routes. A Core NATS subscription receives every subject its subject or pattern matches, and a queue group hands each message to one of its members. A stream stores what its consumers' filter subjects place in it, and a stream a subscription names is there for it. A consumer starts where its deliver policy says, numbers its deliveries, and fills every key of the JetStream context. A JetStream delivery is acknowledged, redelivered, terminated or held for a delay as on a server, and one left unsettled comes back after its ack_wait. A Core NATS delivery has no acknowledgement and is never redelivered. A request to a subject nobody reads fails at once with "no responders". It refuses what a server refuses: a subject with whitespace, a header with no NATS form, a message over the 1 MiB payload limit, a JetStream publish no stream stores, an expectation that does not hold, and every publish after the broker shut down. What only a server has is for a live test: a stream's own subject list and limits, a stream the server lacks, max_ack_pending, authentication and TLS, and the connect itself. A publish through the harness returns once every handler it woke has settled, a reply included. The assertions that follow read finished state.

The dependency line: [dev-dependencies] ruststream-nats = { version = "0.7", features = ["testing"] } The tests publish a payment and read how the handler settled it. TestApp::start_live runs the same test body against a running NATS server, for what only a server has. It connects the broker through its ordinary connect, so startup dials the server and every JetStream subscription looks up its stream there. The body is the one an in-process test runs; only the start call differs. A publish, settle and advance wait on the real clock until every subscription has handled what was published to it. The wait lasts ten seconds at most, and start_live_within sets another bound. The live mode is for what the in-process mode leaves to the server: a stream's own subject list and limits, a stream the server lacks failing startup, max_ack_pending, authentication and TLS, and the timing of the connect. A stream is the server's state, and the server keeps what earlier runs left in it. So a test creates the stream through an admin connection's jetstream before the app starts, replacing a leftover, and deletes it afterwards. In the example, live::url returns the server's address from NATS_TEST_URL, and the test returns early without one, so cargo test passes on a machine with no server. A job that stood a server up sets RUSTSTREAM_REQUIRE_LIVE=1, and a missing address then fails the test instead of skipping it. The repository's stand is docker-compose.test.yml, a NATS server with JetStream that just brokers-up starts.

The two tests share one body: one in process, one against the server at NATS_TEST_URL. Это руководство завершает доставки JetStream исходом обработчика, подбирает ack_wait для медленных обработчиков, обрабатывает сообщение, доставленное дважды, и показывает, чего не обещает Core NATS. Обработчик завершает свою доставку значением, которое возвращает, а рантайм отправляет ответ серверу после обработчика. На консьюмере JetStream каждый исход - это подтверждение, на которое действует сервер: Исход Что получает сервер Что делает сервер ack +ACK забывает сообщение для этого консьюмера retry -NAK сразу доставляет его повторно retry_after(delay) -NAK с задержкой придерживает его и доставляет повторно после задержки drop +TERM больше никогда его не доставляет нет исхода ничего доставляет его повторно после ack_wait Повторная доставка сохраняет порядковый номер сообщения в стриме, а сервер считает его доставки. Пример - платёжный сервис. Он списывает авторизованные платежи через банк и сообщает о каждом списании на панель мониторинга.

Макросы Вручную src/main.rs /// How long a busy bank asks its callers to wait. const BACKOFF: Duration = Duration::from_secs(30); #[derive(Debug, PartialEq, Serialize, Deserialize, Outgoing)] #[outgoing(name = "payments.authorized")] struct Payment { id: u64, card: String, amount_cents: u64, } #[derive(Debug, PartialEq, Serialize, Deserialize, Outgoing)] #[outgoing(name = "payments.captured")] struct Captured { payment: u64, amount_cents: u64, } #[subscriber( JetStreamSubject::new("payments.authorized", "PAYMENTS") .durable("capture") .ack_wait(NonZeroDuration::from_secs(nonzero!(60))), reply )] async fn capture( payment: &Payment, Ctx(delivered): Ctx<Delivered>, State(bank): State<Arc<Bank>>, ) -> Result<Captured, HandlerOutcome> { if delivered.is_some_and(|count| count > 1) { tracing::info!(payment.id, ?delivered, "payment delivered again"); } match bank.capture(payment).await { Ok(()) => Ok(Captured { payment: payment.id, amount_cents: payment.amount_cents, }), // Past the rate limit: the server holds the payment and delivers it after the delay. Err(Refusal::Busy) => Err(HandlerOutcome::retry_after(BACKOFF)), // No answer: the server delivers the payment again at once. Err(Refusal::Unavailable) => Err(HandlerOutcome::retry()), // The server never delivers a terminated payment again. Err(Refusal::Declined) => { tracing::warn!(payment.id, "card declined, payment terminated"); Err(HandlerOutcome::drop()) } } } src/main.rs /// How long a busy bank asks its callers to wait. const BACKOFF: Duration = Duration::from_secs(30); #[derive(Debug, PartialEq, Serialize, Deserialize, JsonSchema)] #[schemars(crate = "ruststream::schemars")] struct Payment { id: u64, card: String, amount_cents: u64, } impl OutgoingDestination for Payment { type Form = FixedName; const DESTINATION: &'static str = "payments.authorized"; } impl MessageHeaders for Payment { type Contract = NoHeaders; } impl MessageInfo for Payment { const NAME: &'static str = "Payment"; } #[derive(Debug, PartialEq, Serialize, Deserialize, JsonSchema)] #[schemars(crate = "ruststream::schemars")] struct Captured { payment: u64, amount_cents: u64, } impl OutgoingDestination for Captured { type Form = FixedName; const DESTINATION: &'static str = "payments.captured"; } impl MessageHeaders for Captured { type Contract = NoHeaders; } impl MessageInfo for Captured { const NAME: &'static str = "Captured"; } struct Capture; impl Handle<Payment, Captured, (), JetStreamContext, Clients> for Capture { async fn handle( &self, payment: &Payment, _outs: &(), ctx: &mut Context<'_, JetStreamContext, Clients>, ) -> Result<Captured, HandlerOutcome> { let delivered = ctx.context(DELIVERED); if delivered.is_some_and(|count| count > 1) { tracing::info!(payment.id, ?delivered, "payment delivered again"); } match ctx.state().bank.capture(payment).await { Ok(()) => Ok(Captured { payment: payment.id, amount_cents: payment.amount_cents, }), // Past the rate limit: the server holds the payment and delivers it after the delay. Err(Refusal::Busy) => Err(HandlerOutcome::retry_after(BACKOFF)), // No answer: the server delivers the payment again at once. Err(Refusal::Unavailable) => Err(HandlerOutcome::retry()), // The server never delivers a terminated payment again. Err(Refusal::Declined) => { tracing::warn!(payment.id, "card declined, payment terminated"); Err(HandlerOutcome::drop()) } } } } Банк отвечает четырьмя способами, и каждому нужен свой исход. Списание возвращает Captured: рантайм публикует его как ответ и затем подтверждает платёж. Busy значит, что лимит запросов банка исчерпан, поэтому платёж ждёт на сервере 30 секунд. Unavailable значит, что банк не ответил, поэтому платёж возвращается сразу. Declined значит, что списать с карты нельзя. Новая попытка получит тот же ответ, поэтому доставка платежа прекращается. retry без предела возвращает платёж бесконечно. Руководство Переобработка и недоставленные сообщения добавляет предел и субъект для недоставленных сообщений.

JetStream доставляет сообщения at-least-once. Платёж возвращается после retry, после истечения ack_wait и после остановки процесса, который не успел завершить его доставку. Поэтому обработчик видит некоторые платежи дважды, и его работа должна допускать повтор. Здесь банк принимает идентификатор платежа как ключ идемпотентности и списывает повторный платёж один раз. Ctx<Delivered> - счётчик доставок сервера, на первой доставке он равен 1. capture пишет в журнал платёж, который видит снова.

Сервер ждёт исхода ack_wait: 30 секунд, если дескриптор не задаёт другое значение. Затем он доставляет сообщение повторно, хотя первый обработчик может ещё работать. capture задаёт 60 секунд, больше самого долгого ответа банка. Задайте ack_wait больше худшего времени обработчика, и две доставки никогда не пересекутся. Истёкший ack_wait тоже считается доставкой для предела попыток.

Макросы Вручную src/main.rs #[subscriber("payments.captured")] async fn refresh(captured: &Captured) -> HandlerOutcome { tracing::info!(captured.payment, "dashboard refreshed"); HandlerOutcome::ack() } src/main.rs struct Refresh; impl Handle<Captured, (), (), (), Clients> for Refresh { fn handle( &self, captured: &Captured, _outs: &(), _ctx: &mut Context<'_, (), Clients>, ) -> impl Future<Output = Result<(), HandlerOutcome>> { tracing::info!(captured.payment, "dashboard refreshed"); ready(Ok(())) } } refresh читает списания из субъекта Core NATS. Core NATS доставляет at-most-once, и подтверждения в нём нет. Завершение доставки Core возвращает AckError::Unsupported, и рантайм пишет это в журнал как предупреждение. Сообщение Core, которое потерял процесс, пропадает, и ничто его не вернёт. Панель может пропустить обновление, потому что следующее списание снова её обновит. Платёж пропасть не может, поэтому платежи проходят через стрим.

Макросы Вручную src/main.rs #[ruststream::app] fn app() -> impl App<State = Clients> { RustStream::new(AppInfo::new("payments", "0.1.0")) .on_startup(async move |()| Ok::<_, Infallible>(Clients::default())) .with_broker(NatsBroker::new("nats://localhost:4222"), |b| { b.include(capture); b.include(refresh); }) } src/main.rs fn app() -> impl App<State = Clients> { RustStream::new(AppInfo::new("payments", "0.1.0")) .on_startup(async move |()| Ok::<_, Infallible>(Clients::default())) .with_broker(NatsBroker::new("nats://localhost:4222"), |b| { b.include( subscriber( JetStreamSubject::new("payments.authorized", "PAYMENTS") .durable("capture") .ack_wait(NonZeroDuration::from_secs(nonzero!(60))), Capture, ) .reply() .build(), ); b.include(subscriber("payments.captured", Refresh).build()); }) } fn main() -> ExitCode { run_main(app) } Клиент банка - состояние приложения, его открывают один раз при запуске. Обработчик пакетов завершает весь пакет одним исходом или каждое сообщение отдельно, если возвращает Vec<HandlerOutcome>. Тесты в файле примера запускают приложение внутри процесса с остановленными часами, поэтому 30 секунд Busy проходят мгновенно.
Это руководство устанавливает ruststream-nats, запускает локальный сервер NATS и первый сервис на нём.

Фича macros даёт атрибуты, json - кодек по умолчанию, а logging выводит журнал сервиса в терминал. ruststream-nats - брокер NATS. У крейта брокера две фичи, обе выключены по умолчанию: Фича Что она даёт testing NATS внутри процесса, на котором работает TestApp asyncapi привязки NATS в генерируемом документе AsyncAPI Крейт построен на клиенте async-nats. Он написан на Rust и шифрует соединение через rustls, поэтому сборке не нужны системные библиотеки.

Для разработки достаточно одного сервера NATS с JetStream: compose.yaml services: nats: image: nats:2-alpine command: ["-js"] ports: - "4222:4222" docker compose up -d Сервер слушает localhost:4222. Флаг -js включает JetStream. С его стримами работают руководства, начиная со Стримов и консьюмеров. Примеры публикуют сообщения утилитой командной строки NATS nats.

Макросы Вручную src/main.rs #[derive(Debug, PartialEq, Deserialize)] struct Order { id: u64, amount_cents: u64, } #[subscriber("orders.created")] async fn take_order(order: &Order) -> HandlerOutcome { if order.amount_cents == 0 { tracing::warn!(order.id, "order without an amount dropped"); return HandlerOutcome::drop(); } tracing::info!(order.id, order.amount_cents, "order taken"); HandlerOutcome::ack() } #[ruststream::app] fn app() -> impl App { RustStream::new(AppInfo::new("orders", "0.1.0")).with_broker( NatsBroker::new("nats://localhost:4222"), |b| { b.include(take_order); }, ) } src/main.rs #[derive(Debug, PartialEq, Deserialize, JsonSchema)] #[schemars(crate = "ruststream::schemars")] struct Order { id: u64, amount_cents: u64, } struct TakeOrder; impl Handle<Order> for TakeOrder { fn handle( &self, order: &Order, _outs: &(), _ctx: &mut Context<'_>, ) -> impl Future<Output = Result<(), HandlerOutcome>> { if order.amount_cents == 0 { tracing::warn!(order.id, "order without an amount dropped"); return ready(Err(HandlerOutcome::drop())); } tracing::info!(order.id, order.amount_cents, "order taken"); ready(Ok(())) } } fn app() -> impl App { RustStream::new(AppInfo::new("orders", "0.1.0")).with_broker( NatsBroker::new("nats://localhost:4222"), |b| { b.include(subscriber("orders.created", TakeOrder).build()); }, ) } fn main() -> ExitCode { run_main(app) } take_order читает заказы в JSON из субъекта Core NATS orders.created. Заказ с суммой он принимает, а заказ без суммы отбрасывает. NatsBroker::new принимает адрес сервера и только запоминает его. Соединение открывается при запуске сервиса. #[ruststream::app] превращает app в main. В ручной форме то же делает run_main. Запустите сервис: cargo run -- run Опубликуйте заказ из другого терминала: nats pub orders.created '{"id":1,"amount_cents":1250}' Сервис пишет в журнал order taken с номером заказа. В Core NATS нет подтверждения, поэтому для каждого заказа в журнале есть и ack / nack failed: рантайм сообщает, что завершить доставку не удалось. Руководство Подтверждение и гарантии доставки объясняет, когда это важно и как стрим завершает каждое сообщение. Ctrl+C останавливает сервис. cargo generate создаёт такой же сервис с роутером: cargo generate --git https://github.com/powersemmi/ruststream-nats templates/nats --name my-service Шаблон templates/nats-js создаёт сервис, который читает стрим через durable-консьюмер.

В файле примера есть и два теста. Каждый запускает то же app через TestApp::start, публикует заказ и проверяет, как take_order завершил его доставку. Там NatsBroker подключается к NATS внутри процесса, поэтому тестам не нужен сервер: cargo test Руководство Тестирование сервиса на NATS разбирает такие тесты и то, что моделирует NATS внутри процесса.

Сервис на async-nats сам пишет цикл для каждой подписки и публикует сообщения вручную. Вот куда переходит каждая часть в RustStream: async-nats RustStream async_nats::connect или ConnectOptions::connect NatsBroker::new и with_options для ConnectOptions client.subscribe и цикл while let Some(message) обработчик #[subscriber("subject")] client.queue_subscribe CoreSubject::queue_group (Субъекты, шаблоны и очереди) serde_json::from_slice(&message.payload) тип параметра обработчика, который декодирует кодек client.publish ответ или параметр Out, отправленный через политику Publish client.request request на слоте Out<impl RequestReply, _> (Запрос и ответ) create_consumer на стриме и цикл messages() JetStreamSubject (Стримы и консьюмеры) message.ack(), AckKind::Nak, AckKind::Term исход обработчика: ack, retry, retry_after, drop (Подтверждение и гарантии доставки) jetstream.publish и его подтверждение JetStreamPublish (Публикация в стримы)

В промышленном кластере несколько серверов, он требует от сервиса назвать себя и работает через TLS. Всё это - настройки ConnectOptions из async-nats, которые брокер принимает до установки соединения.

src/main.rs /// Where the cluster is and who the service is, as the deployment provides them. struct Deployment { /// One server address or a comma-separated list. servers: String, /// The contents of the service's `.creds` file: its user JWT and its `NKey` seed. creds: String, /// The certificate authority that signed the servers' certificates. ca: PathBuf, } impl Deployment { fn from_env() -> io::Result<Self> { let var = |name: &str| { env::var(name).map_err(|_| io::Error::new(io::ErrorKind::NotFound, name.to_owned())) }; Ok(Self { servers: var("NATS_SERVERS")?, creds: fs::read_to_string(var("NATS_CREDS")?)?, ca: var("NATS_CA")?.into(), }) } } fn broker(deployment: Deployment) -> io::Result<NatsBroker> { let options = ConnectOptions::with_credentials(&deployment.creds)? .add_root_certificates(deployment.ca) .require_tls(true) .name("orders") .connection_timeout(Duration::from_secs(10)); Ok(NatsBroker::new(deployment.servers).with_options(options)) } Cargo.toml [dependencies] async-nats = "0.50" Серверы и пути к двум файлам развёртывание передаёт в переменных окружения. NatsBroker::new принимает один адрес или список через запятую, и клиент выбирает из них тот, к которому подключится. with_options добавляет ConnectOptions и по-прежнему никуда не подключается. Файл .creds содержит JWT пользователя и seed его ключа NKey. Так сервис называет себя в Synadia Cloud и в учётных записях, настроенных через nsc. Приложение читает файл и передаёт его содержимое в ConnectOptions::with_credentials, который сразу его разбирает. ConnectOptions::with_credentials_file читает файл сам, но он асинхронный, а приложение строится в синхронной функции. Если файл не разбирается, сервис останавливается до подключения. Для сервера, настроенного с именем пользователя и паролем, есть ConnectOptions::with_user_and_password, с токеном - with_token, с одним только ключом NKey - with_nkey. add_root_certificates называет центр сертификации, который подписал сертификаты серверов, а require_tls отклоняет соединение без TLS. add_client_certificate добавляет собственный сертификат сервиса, если кластер требует взаимной аутентификации TLS. Файлы сертификатов клиент читает при подключении. name показывает сервис в мониторинге сервера, а connection_timeout ограничивает каждую попытку подключения.

Макросы Вручную src/main.rs #[subscriber( JetStreamSubject::new("orders.placed", "ORDERS").durable("confirmer"), reply )] async fn confirm(order: &Order) -> Confirmation { tracing::info!(order.id, "order confirmed"); Confirmation { order: order.id } } fn service(broker: NatsBroker) -> RustStream { RustStream::new(AppInfo::new("orders", "0.1.0")).with_broker(broker, |b| { b.include(confirm); }) } #[ruststream::app] fn app() -> impl App { let broker = Deployment::from_env() .and_then(broker) .expect("NATS_SERVERS, NATS_CREDS and NATS_CA describe the connection"); service(broker) } src/main.rs struct Confirm; impl Handle<Order, Confirmation> for Confirm { fn handle( &self, order: &Order, _outs: &(), _ctx: &mut Context<'_>, ) -> impl Future<Output = Result<Confirmation, HandlerOutcome>> { tracing::info!(order.id, "order confirmed"); ready(Ok(Confirmation { order: order.id })) } } fn service(broker: NatsBroker) -> RustStream { RustStream::new(AppInfo::new("orders", "0.1.0")).with_broker(broker, |b| { b.include( subscriber( JetStreamSubject::new("orders.placed", "ORDERS").durable("confirmer"), Confirm, ) .reply() .build(), ); }) } fn app() -> RustStream { let broker = Deployment::from_env() .and_then(broker) .expect("NATS_SERVERS, NATS_CREDS and NATS_CA describe the connection"); service(broker) } fn main() -> ExitCode { run_main(app) } app строит брокер из окружения и передаёт его в service, ту же функцию, которую вызывают тесты. Рантайм подключается при запуске. Дальше клиент сам переподключается, когда сервер пропадает, и восстанавливает подписки. Генерируемый документ AsyncAPI указывает хост и порт каждого сервера, но никогда не учётные данные. Клиент, созданный вне фреймворка, например общий с другим кодом процесса, становится подключённым брокером через ConnectedNatsBroker::from_client. В синхронную функцию приложения подходит только обычный NatsBroker, поэтому везде, где настройку можно выразить через with_options, используйте его.

Тесты запускают рабочий service с рабочим broker, которому переданы тестовые учётные данные, через TestApp::start. NATS внутри процесса разбирает адреса так же, как клиент, и никуда не подключается, поэтому учётные данные и путь к сертификату не доходят ни до какого сервера. Второй тест передаёт broker файл .creds, который не разбирается, и ожидает ошибку. Сами аутентификация и TLS работают только на настоящем кластере.

Это руководство публикует ответы и сообщения в стримы JetStream, сохраняет повторное сообщение один раз и отклоняет запись, сделанную по устаревшей версии. Обычная публикация уходит через Core NATS, и никто её не подтверждает. JetStreamPublish ждёт, пока стрим подтвердит каждое сообщение. Поэтому сообщение, которое стрим отклонил, - это ошибка, которую видит обработчик, а не тихая потеря. Пример - сервис заказов. Он подтверждает каждый заказ, архивирует его и хранит историю каждой учётной записи клиента. Стримы, в которые он пишет, уже есть на сервере: nats stream add ORDERS --subjects 'orders.placed' --defaults nats stream add CONFIRMATIONS --subjects 'confirmations.orders' --defaults nats stream add ARCHIVE --subjects 'archive.orders' --defaults nats stream add ACCOUNTS --subjects 'accounts.*' --defaults

Макросы Вручную src/main.rs #[derive(Debug, PartialEq, Serialize, Deserialize, Outgoing)] #[outgoing(name = "confirmations.orders")] struct Confirmation { order: u64, } #[subscriber( JetStreamSubject::new("orders.placed", "ORDERS").durable("confirmer"), reply )] async fn confirm(order: &Order) -> Confirmation { tracing::info!(order.id, "order confirmed"); Confirmation { order: order.id } } src/main.rs #[derive(Debug, PartialEq, Serialize, Deserialize, JsonSchema)] #[schemars(crate = "ruststream::schemars")] struct Confirmation { order: u64, } impl OutgoingDestination for Confirmation { type Form = FixedName; const DESTINATION: &'static str = "confirmations.orders"; } impl MessageHeaders for Confirmation { type Contract = NoHeaders; } impl MessageInfo for Confirmation { const NAME: &'static str = "Confirmation"; } struct Confirm; impl Handle<Order, Confirmation> for Confirm { fn handle( &self, order: &Order, _outs: &(), _ctx: &mut Context<'_>, ) -> impl Future<Output = Result<Confirmation, HandlerOutcome>> { tracing::info!(order.id, "order confirmed"); ready(Ok(Confirmation { order: order.id })) } } confirm отвечает на каждый заказ сообщением Confirmation в confirmations.orders. Приложение ниже отправляет этот ответ через JetStreamPublish::default().expect_stream("CONFIRMATIONS"). expect_stream называет стрим, который должен хранить субъект, и публикация, которую принял бы другой стрим, отклоняется. Заказ подтверждается только после того, как стрим сохранил подтверждение. Если подтверждение отклонено, доставка заказа завершается ошибкой, и заказ возвращается. Субъект ответа лежит вне субъектов ORDERS. Ответ, сохранённый в стриме, который читает обработчик, снова пришёл бы к этому обработчику.

Макросы Вручную src/main.rs #[derive(Debug, PartialEq, Serialize, Deserialize, Outgoing)] #[outgoing(name = "archive.orders")] struct Archived { order: u64, amount_cents: u64, } #[derive(OutSlot)] #[publishes(Archived)] struct Archive; #[subscriber(JetStreamSubject::new("orders.placed", "ORDERS").durable("archiver"))] async fn archive( order: &Order, Out(out): Out<impl Publisher<Options = JetStreamOptions>, Archive>, ) -> HandlerOutcome { let archived = Archived { order: order.id, amount_cents: order.amount_cents, }; // The same id on every delivery of this order: the stream stores the first copy only. if out .message(&archived) .message_id(format!("order-{}", order.id)) .publish() .await .is_err() { return HandlerOutcome::retry(); } HandlerOutcome::ack() } #[subscriber(JetStreamSubject::new("archive.orders", "ARCHIVE").durable("indexer"))] async fn index(archived: &Archived) -> HandlerOutcome { tracing::info!(archived.order, "archived order indexed"); HandlerOutcome::ack() } src/main.rs #[derive(Debug, PartialEq, Serialize, Deserialize, JsonSchema)] #[schemars(crate = "ruststream::schemars")] struct Archived { order: u64, amount_cents: u64, } impl OutgoingDestination for Archived { type Form = FixedName; const DESTINATION: &'static str = "archive.orders"; } impl MessageHeaders for Archived { type Contract = NoHeaders; } impl MessageInfo for Archived { const NAME: &'static str = "Archived"; } struct Archive; impl OutSlot for Archive { const NAME: &'static str = "Archive"; type Destination = Reads; } impl PublishedThrough<Archive> for Archived {} struct ArchiveOrder; impl<Copies> Handle<Order, (), Outs<(Copies,)>> for ArchiveOrder where Copies: OutEntry<Archive, Wire: Publisher<Options = JetStreamOptions>>, { async fn handle( &self, order: &Order, outs: &Outs<(Copies,)>, _ctx: &mut Context<'_>, ) -> Result<(), HandlerOutcome> { let archived = Archived { order: order.id, amount_cents: order.amount_cents, }; // The same id on every delivery of this order: the stream stores the first copy only. if outs .get(Archive) .message(&archived) .message_id(format!("order-{}", order.id)) .publish() .await .is_err() { return Err(HandlerOutcome::retry()); } Ok(()) } } struct Index; impl Handle<Archived> for Index { fn handle( &self, archived: &Archived, _outs: &(), _ctx: &mut Context<'_>, ) -> impl Future<Output = Result<(), HandlerOutcome>> { tracing::info!(archived.order, "archived order indexed"); ready(Ok(())) } } Заказ может быть доставлен дважды, и тогда archive публикует его копию дважды. message_id даёт каждой копии одного заказа один и тот же идентификатор, который передаётся в заголовке Nats-Msg-Id. Стрим сохраняет первую копию и подтверждает повтор, не сохраняя его, поэтому index читает каждый заказ один раз. Стрим помнит идентификаторы в течение своего окна дубликатов: две минуты, если стрим не задаёт другое значение. message_id описывает одно сообщение, поэтому это шаг публикации, а не настройка точки монтирования. Шаги даёт JetStreamPublishSteps из прелюдии крейта. Тело обработчика, которое вызывает такой шаг, ограничивает свой слот типом Out<impl Publisher<Options = JetStreamOptions>, _>. Это ограничение привязывает обработчик к JetStream. Только здесь обработчик называет брокер.

#[subscriber("commands.change-email")] async fn change_email( change: &ChangeEmail, Out(history): Out<impl Publisher<Options = JetStreamOptions>, History>, ) -> HandlerOutcome { let event = EmailChanged { account: change.account, email: change.email.clone(), }; let stored = history .message(&event) .to(format!("accounts.{}", change.account)) .expect_last_subject_sequence(change.version) .publish() .await; if stored.is_err() { tracing::warn!( change.account, change.version, "change made from a stale version refused" ); return HandlerOutcome::drop(); } HandlerOutcome::ack() } src/main.rs /// A change of an account's e-mail, made from the version of the account the client last read: /// the stream sequence of its last event, or 0 for an account with no events yet. #[derive(Debug, PartialEq, Serialize, Deserialize, JsonSchema)] #[schemars(crate = "ruststream::schemars")] struct ChangeEmail { account: u64, version: u64, email: String, } impl OutgoingDestination for ChangeEmail { type Form = FixedName; const DESTINATION: &'static str = "commands.change-email"; } impl MessageHeaders for ChangeEmail { type Contract = NoHeaders; } impl MessageInfo for ChangeEmail { const NAME: &'static str = "ChangeEmail"; } /// An event of an account's history, stored under the account's own subject. #[derive(Debug, PartialEq, Serialize, Deserialize, JsonSchema)] #[schemars(crate = "ruststream::schemars")] struct EmailChanged { account: u64, email: String, } impl OutgoingDestination for EmailChanged { type Form = CallerName; } impl MessageHeaders for EmailChanged { type Contract = NoHeaders; } impl MessageInfo for EmailChanged { const NAME: &'static str = "EmailChanged"; } struct History; impl OutSlot for History { const NAME: &'static str = "History"; type Destination = Reads; } impl PublishedThrough<History> for EmailChanged {} struct ApplyChange; impl<Events> Handle<ChangeEmail, (), Outs<(Events,)>> for ApplyChange where Events: OutEntry<History, Wire: Publisher<Options = JetStreamOptions>>, { async fn handle( &self, change: &ChangeEmail, outs: &Outs<(Events,)>, _ctx: &mut Context<'_>, ) -> Result<(), HandlerOutcome> { let event = EmailChanged { account: change.account, email: change.email.clone(), }; let stored = outs .get(History) .message(&event) .to(format!("accounts.{}", change.account)) .expect_last_subject_sequence(change.version) .publish() .await; if stored.is_err() { tracing::warn!( change.account, change.version, "change made from a stale version refused" ); return Err(HandlerOutcome::drop()); } Ok(()) } } История учётной записи 42 - это субъект стрима accounts.42. Клиент меняет адрес электронной почты учётной записи, опираясь на версию, которую прочитал последней: порядковый номер последнего события учётной записи в стриме. expect_last_subject_sequence заставляет стрим сохранить событие, только если последнее сообщение субъекта всё ещё стоит под этим номером. Два клиента, прочитавшие одну версию, не могут записать оба: вторая запись отклоняется, и change_email её отбрасывает. expect_last_sequence проверяет весь стрим, а не один субъект, а expect_last_message_id - идентификатор последнего сообщения стрима.

Макросы Вручную src/main.rs #[ruststream::app] fn app() -> impl App<State = ()> { RustStream::new(AppInfo::new("orders", "0.1.0")).with_broker( NatsBroker::new("nats://localhost:4222"), |b| { b.include(confirm) .out_reply(JetStreamPublish::default().expect_stream("CONFIRMATIONS")); b.include(archive) .out( Archive, JetStreamPublish::default().expect_stream("ARCHIVE"), ) .build(); b.include(index); b.include(change_email) .out( History, JetStreamPublish::default().expect_stream("ACCOUNTS"), ) .build(); }, ) } src/main.rs fn app() -> impl App<State = ()> { RustStream::new(AppInfo::new("orders", "0.1.0")).with_broker( NatsBroker::new("nats://localhost:4222"), |b| { b.include( subscriber( JetStreamSubject::new("orders.placed", "ORDERS").durable("confirmer"), Confirm, ) .reply() .build(), ) .out_reply(JetStreamPublish::default().expect_stream("CONFIRMATIONS")); b.include( subscriber( JetStreamSubject::new("orders.placed", "ORDERS").durable("archiver"), ArchiveOrder, ) .build(), ) .out( Archive, JetStreamPublish::default().expect_stream("ARCHIVE"), ) .build(); b.include( subscriber( JetStreamSubject::new("archive.orders", "ARCHIVE").durable("indexer"), Index, ) .build(), ); b.include(subscriber("commands.change-email", ApplyChange).build()) .out( History, JetStreamPublish::default().expect_stream("ACCOUNTS"), ) .build(); }, ) } fn main() -> ExitCode { run_main(app) } Каждая публикация JetStream ждёт подтверждения от стрима. Вне доставки хук запуска принимает политику, и publish_ack возвращает это подтверждение: стрим, порядковый номер и то, видело ли сообщение окно дубликатов. Публикация Core NATS подходит там, где потеря сообщения допустима, например для панели мониторинга из руководства Подтверждение и гарантии доставки. Тесты в файле примера запускают приложение внутри процесса: стрим внутри процесса проверяет идентификаторы сообщений и ожидания так же, как сервер.

Это руководство отправляет запрос другому сервису через NATS и ждёт ответа, отвечает на запросы в их инбокс, обрабатывает запрос, на который никто не отвечает, и масштабирует отвечающую сторону. NATS сам сопоставляет ответ с запросом. Запрос содержит инбокс, уникальный для него субъект, и ответ публикуется в этот инбокс. Пример - два сервиса в одном приложении. Сервис цен отвечает на вопросы о ценах, а сервис заказов спрашивает у него цену каждого заказа.

Макросы Вручную src/main.rs /// What the orders service asks the pricing service. #[derive(Debug, PartialEq, Serialize, Deserialize)] struct Ask { sku: String, } /// The pricing service's answer, sent to the inbox of the request. #[derive(Debug, PartialEq, Serialize, Deserialize, Outgoing)] struct Price { sku: String, cents: u64, } /// The catalogue the pricing service answers from. fn price_of(sku: &str) -> Option<u64> { match sku { "book" => Some(1250), "pen" => Some(150), _ => None, } } #[derive(OutSlot)] #[publishes(Price)] struct Answers; Это руководство переобрабатывает доставку сразу или позже, ограничивает число попыток и сохраняет то, что раз за разом не обрабатывается, в стриме для недоставленных сообщений: на консьюмере стрима, на субъекте Core и на шаблоне. В NATS нет механизма недоставленных сообщений. JetStream умеет ограничивать число доставок сообщения, но последнюю доставку никуда не отправляет. Поэтому предел и субъект для недоставленных сообщений объявляет точка монтирования, а фреймворк применяет их к обеим моделям. Пример - платёжный сервис, который проводит платежи и отправляет возвраты через банк. Недоставленные сообщения он хранит в отдельном стриме: nats stream add PAYMENTS --subjects 'payments.settle' --defaults nats stream add DEAD --subjects 'dead.*' --defaults

Стрим хранит сообщения, опубликованные в его субъекты, каждое под своим порядковым номером. Консьюмер читает стрим в своём темпе и подтверждает сообщения по одному. Пример - интернет-магазин. Он исполняет новые заказы, показывает каждое событие заказа на панели мониторинга и сверяет оплаченные заказы с банком.

Стрим - это состояние сервера. Сервис находит его при запуске и никогда не создаёт, поэтому создайте его один раз утилитой командной строки NATS: nats stream add ORDERS --subjects 'orders.*' --defaults ORDERS хранит каждое сообщение, опубликованное в orders.created, orders.paid и любой другой субъект, к которому подходит orders.*. Обычная публикация в такой субъект сохраняется, кто бы её ни отправил. Если подписка называет стрим, которого на сервере нет, сервис не запускается.
